main_text.p: infeliciter ; neuter eloqventiæ vernaculæ limites egressus est. Quædam Cicero adolescens græce periclitatus est, sed umbratilem exercitationem potius prolusit, quam serio dixit ; quapropter ipse omnia ejusmodi obliteravit, nec unquam ab umbra in aprieum eduxit. Absolutam perfectionem mortalibus invidisse natura videtur, ut cùm divinæ & humanæ naturæ participes sint, divinam ita cogitent, ut humanæ non sint immemores. Verùm quidquid tibi libuerit, natura insolenter indulgens tibi concedit, omnia quæ ferre jubet contra morem felicissime unam & eamdem tellurem; cui igitur potius gratuler, anceps sum, tibi an S. Augustino, an Ecclesiæ Catholicæ ; tibi, qui fortissimum civem ex hostium manibus fortissime ereptum, reipublicæ Catholicæ reddidisti : S. Augustino, quod calumniæ, quibus sanctissima ipsius doctrina ab hæreticis appetitur ac obtenebratur, eloquentiæ tuæ fulmine tactæ qenitus[?] evanuerint: Ecclesiæ, quæ celeberrimum doctorem suum, hostium contume-

page.notes: Line 2: "Quædam Cicero" is printed without a space after Quædam in the scan; kept as the spacing shows. Line 4 "aprieum" as printed in the scan (likely apricum); the e/c is doubtful, so check it. Line 14 "invidisse" printed with a long-s form; written as s. "qenitus" (line 27): the first letter looks like a damaged p; marked [?]. Line 31: "suum,hostium" has no space after the comma, as printed. Last line "contume-" is the end of the page; the word continues on the next page. Right and left edges show rule lines and scan edge, not printed text.
